sources: Indian Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal (X statement); UKMTO advisory; Times Kuwait
fault_line: Who fired — and who keeps sailing through? Two tankers hit in six days in the world's most important oil lane: does traffic keep flowing or do insurers and crews say enough?

sections.what_happened: M/T Al Dasma (Kuwait-flagged oil product tanker, 21 Indian seafarers) struck by unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 21; UKMTO tracked the strike 11 nm west of Bukha, Oman; fire aboard extinguished; all crew safe. Second tanker hit in six days (MT ST 3 struck Oct 16, 15 Indian seafarers, also safe). NO attribution to any actor on record — attacker unknown.
sections.what_verified: IANS reporting carried by 4+ independent outlets; minister's direct X quote; UKMTO advisory location detail; Times Kuwait fire detail. MT ST 3 precedent (Oct 16) confirmed by same minister days earlier.
sections.what_disputed: Iranian outlets (via relays) frame US-Israeli strikes as targeting civilian sites — attacker identity is contested; do NOT attribute the projectile to Iran on record. Casualty/strike details rely on official statements, not independent inspection of the vessel.
sections.why_matters: VERIFIED shipping-chokepoint disruption — elevation trigger. Frame the cadence (2 strikes, 6 days) with the UKMTO position data; carry the known-unknown: no named attacker. Pocketbook angle: freight/insurance repricing as the silent tax on every viewer. Carries the Hormuz by the Numbers franchise entry.
